purpose: Curated high-bar reference memory for comparative design reasoning. References teach mechanisms and quality thresholds; they are never templates, style-transfer targets, or permission to copy proprietary expression.
selection_policy: Prefer products with a strong, legible design thesis and mature interaction craft.
Store mechanism lessons separately from brand expression and exact visual appearance.
Re-inspect live first-party sources when a current implementation detail materially affects a decision.
Use multiple references when making a consequential aesthetic choice so one brand cannot become the house style.
A reference loses authority when its mechanism conflicts with the product's users, platform, accessibility, risk, or information density.

references.name: Stripe
references.anti_copy: Do not reproduce Stripe gradients, illustrations, layouts, typography, or page composition; abstract only the mechanism that precision and trust can coexist with distinctive brand expression.
references.refresh_policy: Treat live visual details as high-drift; inspect current first-party surfaces before citing a concrete treatment.

references.name: Linear
references.anti_copy: Do not turn every B2B application into a dark Linear clone; use the reference to study prioritization, speed, hierarchy and command reachability.
references.refresh_policy: Verify current product behavior when exact navigation or command mechanics matter.

references.name: Notion
references.anti_copy: Do not copy Notion's block language or neutral visual identity by default; learn how chrome can recede behind user content.
references.refresh_policy: Inspect live editor behavior for current interaction claims.

references.name: Framer
references.anti_copy: Do not reuse Framer's specific panel arrangement or visual language as a generic editor template; extract tool/context/preview coordination principles.
references.refresh_policy: Editor mechanics are high-drift; verify current first-party documentation or product behavior.

references.name: Apple platform experiences
references.anti_copy: Do not paste Apple aesthetics onto web or non-Apple platforms; separate platform convention from transferable craft principles.
references.refresh_policy: First-party platform guidance is authoritative for current Apple conventions and must be refreshed when platform behavior changes.

references.name: Airbnb
references.anti_copy: Do not reproduce Airbnb cards, iconography or marketplace structure unless product semantics independently demand them.
references.refresh_policy: Re-check live marketplace flows before relying on concrete interaction details.

references.name: Arc browser
references.anti_copy: Do not assume sidebar-first browser conventions generalize to unrelated products; use Arc as evidence that familiar chrome can be reconsidered when the task model supports it.
references.refresh_policy: Product availability and interaction details can change; verify before concrete adoption.

references.name: Vercel
references.anti_copy: Do not use monochrome minimalism as an automatic developer-tool style; study the alignment between product semantics, status information and restrained presentation.
references.refresh_policy: Verify current dashboard/docs details when implementation-specific.

references.name: Ramp
references.anti_copy: Do not inherit Ramp's brand system or exact data composition; study how high-consequence financial tasks can remain fast and legible.
references.refresh_policy: Refresh current product claims and UI before concrete comparison.

references.name: Raycast
references.anti_copy: Do not force command-palette interaction onto novice or touch-first audiences; transfer the command registry and discoverability logic only when task frequency supports it.
references.refresh_policy: Inspect current extension and command behavior when exact mechanics matter.

references.name: Visual Studio Code
references.anti_copy: Do not create an Activity Bar, Explorer and Panel merely because an application is complex; learn how distinct zones own distinct command and context scopes.
references.refresh_policy: Use current first-party documentation for exact workbench conventions and settings behavior.

references.name: Canva
references.anti_copy: Do not copy Canva's asset panels or consumer visual language; study how many capabilities remain approachable through progressive disclosure and context.
references.refresh_policy: Creative-tool surfaces change frequently; verify exact behavior live before adoption.

references.name: CapCut
references.anti_copy: Do not reproduce CapCut's timeline, asset browser or branding; abstract the coordination between media, timeline, tools, preview, inspector and export lifecycle.
references.refresh_policy: Verify current editor behavior because tool placement and feature sets drift quickly.

references.name: Adobe Spectrum
references.anti_copy: Do not treat Spectrum components as a universal aesthetic; use first-party guidance to study robust system behavior and application-frame mechanics.
references.refresh_policy: Re-check first-party Spectrum guidance for current component and platform decisions.
